newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telepizza confident of shareholder backing.
newsitem.headline: Telepizza confident of shareholder backing.

text.p: Spain's Telepizza is confident that shareholders will back its move to transfer 1996 profits over to reserves in order to finance investments, foregoing a dividend payment.
Chairman Leopoldo Fernandez Pujals said on Friday: "The dividend this year would be so small that it would be insignificant."
Speaking to journalists at a meeting, Fernandez estimated that only around one or two percent of the firm is owned by small shareholders.
Larger institutional investors, around 10 percent of whom are from the United States, fully backed the move.
The annual shareholders' meeting is provisionally set for the end of April.
"This is logical in view of our outlook," he said, which was of a small rapidly-growing company.
But Fernandez added the company did not yet know whether the plan to buy Pizza World, which would cost a maximum 1.9 billion pesetas, would require the company taking on debt.
As regards prospects for 1997, Telepizza's results would be "better than some analysts expect," he added. The firm posted profits of 1.70 billion pesetas in 1996.
Telepizza plans to open around 90 outlets per year for the medium term, and, if it goes ahead, the Pizza World purchase would add 60-70 outlets.
